This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. The U.S. government is restricting Chinese
companies from accessing American AI technology through overseas data centers. NPR's Katie McHugh
reports. While there have been export restrictions on physical trips to China for several years,
a loophole existed that allowed Chinese companies to gain remote access to American AI technology.
The new rule replaces a Biden-era framework to regulate global access to advanced AI chips,
which the Trump administration never enforced. The move comes amid the fallout from
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Huang had lobbied President Trump to
relax chip export restrictions to China. Huang resigned from Nvidia last week. Katie McHugh,
NPR News, New York. At least six people were injured after Ukraine launched a large-scale
drone attack on targets in Russia and the occupied territories overnight. NPR's Charles
Maine's reports from Moscow. The strikes come as Ukraine responds to Russia's assault on civilian
energy infrastructure ahead of the winter months. What appeared to mark the largest combined drone
counterattack by Kiev since Russia launched its full-scale invasion nearly five years ago.
Russia said its air defenses successfully intercepted the Ukrainian barrage,
a claim that stood at odds with reports of damage at several large Russian oil and industrial
facilities. Also hit the lone bridge linking occupied Crimea to mainland Russia, a project
seen as a physical symbol of Russia's hold over the peninsula. It illegally annexed from Ukraine
back in 2014. The local Moscow-backed authorities reported a halt to traffic along the bridge.
The Kremlin later dismissed the damage as minor. Charles Maine's NPR News, Moscow.
The Trump administration is pushing for billions of dollars to update the aging air traffic control
system after a router issue caused a nationwide grounding of planes last week. Democrats are
questioning how previous funds have been spent and why the new request is so high. Transportation
Secretary Sean Duffy says that the problem began with a contractor replacing old wiring,
causing system overloads. Maryland Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen says he knows he's the
underdog in his fight to unseat Chuck Schumer as Senate Democratic leader,
that he says he can get the support he needs to win. NPR's Eric McDaniel has the story.
By some measures, Chuck Schumer is the most unpopular politician in America.
Many voters don't like his party either. Only some 40 percent hold a favorable view of Democrats.
But they did just give the Senate minority leader and his party huge governing majorities.
And Senator Van Hollen actually tells NPR that's part of a larger plea for something new.
People around the country are looking for change, and my colleagues are listening to people around
the country. Public pressure could move senators into Van Hollen's column, but picking the Senate
majority leader is a closed-door closed ballot election, and it's not until December 1st anything
could happen. Eric McDaniel, NPR News, Washington. Major U.S. stock indexes fell today. The S&P 500
fell nearly 2 percent for its third straight loss. This is NPR News from Washington.
The population of one of the world's rarest whales has fallen after trending upward in recent years.
The North Atlantic right whales were decimated by centuries of commercial whaling that mostly
ended in the 1930s. The consortium of scientists says there are now only 382 of them. That's about
a 2 percent decline from last year's estimate, which showed a recent slow but steady climb in
the whales population. How much we can sleep can have a powerful influence on our weight,
NPR's Maria Godoy reports. Adults are supposed to sleep seven to nine hours a night.
Many of us don't hit that mark. Research has shown insufficient sleep can lead to weight gain,
primarily by driving us to eat more, especially later in the day,
says Seth Creasy of the University of Colorado and Schutz. If you're getting less sleep,
you're eating on average. You know, if you pull across studies, it's around 300 calories more
that you're eating per day. Imaging studies have shown that when we're short on sleep,
activity ramps up in areas of the brain involved in pleasure and reward,
making it harder to resist sweet and salty snacks. But research has also linked eating fruits and
vegetables high in fiber and other nutrients to better sleep and fewer awakenings at night.
Maria Godoy, NPR News. NASA's Voyager 1 is about to become humanity's first object to reach one
light day from Earth on Wednesday. At that point, its radio signals will take precisely 24 hours
traveling at the speed of light to reach Earth. Its twin, Voyager 2, is expected to reach one
light day in 2035, launched in 1977. The Voyagers have been pushing deeper into space after visiting
the outer planets. This is NPR. This message comes from Mattress Firm. Sharing a bed should not mean
